messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
a faint new vibration appears under load while you are handling A belt-driven feeder beside a noisy machine. You have only a few minutes before someone else needs it. How do you approach it?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "\"Faint. Slow.\" You check the belt. \"One mark. Likely.\" You shift the feeder beneath the machine, but keep the vibration under the belt."}, {"id": "R014", "response": "i lift the load and listen under the belt. the vibration stays, so i write the time on my palm. “i have it under the feeder, not a fault.” i leave the machine running and leave the vibration in my hand. “i can write the time on my wrist.”"}, {"id": "R015", "response": "I move the belt under the machine. No—the vibration is not under it. I put my hand on the spindle. No. I press it down. Then I lift the feeder. The vibration stops. I check the belt. I leave it under the machine."}, {"id": "R016", "response": "the belt comes first. the vibration knocks my shin. i press the feeder hard. the belt slides under the machine. i turn the feeder. the vibration dies. the feeder stays. i press the belt under the machine. the vibration dies. i go back to the feeder."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "1. stop. 2. check the watch. slow. 3. i crouch. 4. touch the belt. 5. check the dust. 6. check the machine. 7. one hand on the plate. 8. i keep it tidy."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "I stop the feeder. the vibration catches my wrist. i move the belt closer, then stop. i rub the gear with my thumb. “same sound.” i leave the feed aside and pocket the loose bolt. “not enough time.”"}, {"id": "R019", "response": "i pull the feeder closer and touch the belt with my thumbnail. the vibration goes off, but i keep my hand still on the belt. i move the feeder to the wrong side, then put it back in the rack. i wait a second, then put it back in the rack again."}, {"id": "R020", "response": "i move the feeder slowly and keep the vibration close. i stop when i hear the same creak. i keep the belt turned away from the machine and write down the date on a loose sketch."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "i stop moving and keep the feeder beside the machine. i tap the seam with my thumbnail, feeling for the faint scratch that marks the old vibration. i leave the feeder alone and keep the belt-driven feeder in the corner."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "i move the feeder under the noise and place the vibration on the belt-driven gear. i keep the gear’s rim visible and the feeder inside. i keep the noise level low and the vibration steady. i watch the gear’s gear indicator and press the feeder once when it stops."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "i hold the feeder with both hands and tap the metal with my fingertip. the vibration spreads over the edge, so i tap the belt once and leave a faint mark beside it. “i’m holding the feeder,” i say, and put the feeder beside the noise."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "you put the feeder on the step. the vibration stays there. you look at the machine. “quiet.” you leave the belt alone. “not the feeder.”"}]
